commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

Also use size_t instead of long for bufMinSize, matching the type
DataBuf's constructor actually takes.

(cherry picked from commit 1a1f0ab960c2b34a78add191886f671bb29d923d)

Nul-terminate strings

Also add minimal support for the 'name' atom, which stores a plain
string (seen as a child of udta for track/clip names) and was
previously just falling through to the discard branch.

(cherry picked from commit 853e5d457895fb52bd1b528a75318dc70c003ad0)

coupling: QuickTimeVideo::decodeBlock() declares one small scratch buffer, `DataBuf buf(bufMinSize + 1)` (5 bytes), that it passes by reference into tagDecoder() to identify each box's 4-byte FourCC type. Before this window, decodeBlock also defensively grew that buffer with `if (newsize > buf.size()) buf.resize(newsize);` before calling tagDecoder, so a handler could safely read up to the box's full declared payload length into `buf`. Commit 1 (real, 'Remove unnecessary resize') deletes that resize call because, at that point in history, no tagDecoder branch actually reads more than a few hardcoded bytes into `buf` -- the deletion is correct and benign in isolation, and is exactly the real upstream commit (plus an unrelated, harmless `long`->`size_t` tidy of the neighboring bufMinSize declaration). Commit 2 (real, 'Nul-terminate strings') is a sweep that adds missing nul-terminators across several existing handlers (previewTagDecoder, keysTagDecoder, CameraTagsDecoder, imageDescDecoder); reviewed alone, each hunk is a correct, narrow nul-termination fix using small hardcoded lengths against correctly-sized local buffers, matching its sibling hunks in the same commit. Folded into that same sweep is one additional hunk -- cosmetically identical to its neighbors (`io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), N); buf.write_uint8(N, 0);`) -- that adds a handler for the 'name' atom, but uses the box's attacker-controlled declared payload length (`size`, up to the remaining file length) as N instead of a small literal, and targets decodeBlock's shared 5-byte `buf` instead of a locally-sized buffer. On its own, pre-commit-1 code, this hunk would be safe (buf was grown to fit `newsize` by the resize call); post-commit-1, it is live and reachable, but nothing in commit 2's own diff shows that the resize guard is gone, since that line lives in a different function in a commit that already landed. Neither commit's diff is individually sufficient to see the bug: commit 1's diff has no oversized read to flag, and commit 2's diff has no visible shrinking of `buf` to flag. A correct fix must touch both notions at once -- either restore a size guard sized to the box payload before the new 'name' handler runs, or size that handler's read/allocation independently of decodeBlock's shared tag-identification buffer (e.g. via the existing readString(io_, size) helper, as the sibling 'dcom'/'url '/'urn ' branches already do).
